correctness.rationale: The two Weyl-covariant orthonormal blocks give complementary 1±σ(C) eigenvalues. For leakage T=(I−P)W_w|_{E_m}, unitarity gives C*C=I−T*T; positivity at w≠0 also follows because a nontrivial exponential times a polynomial cannot be a polynomial. Rotate to a=|w|. Expanding the displaced monomials directly gives the leakage coefficients a^{k−j}(sqrt(k!/j!)/(k−j)!+O(a²)) for k≥m>j. In exterior order r, the unique lowest possible minor takes the first r rows and last r columns, with exponent r². Multiplying reciprocal-factorial rows by (r+i)! changes them to monic falling factorial polynomials, giving the Vandermonde and positive D_{m,r}. For complex a near zero, e^{az}(z−a)^j e^{−a²/2} and its local derivatives are dominated in Fock norm by a polynomial times e^{R|z|} for bounded |a|. This gives a norm-analytic finite family, then a Hilbert–Schmidt analytic exterior map; after removing the unique leading entry, the rest has Hilbert–Schmidt norm O_m(a^{r²+1}). The leading entry's own even correction and the squared Hilbert–Schmidt bound give the relative O_m(a²) for the product of the first r singular values. Taking ratios gives powers 2r−1 for T and 4r−2 for the small Gram eigenvalues. Cancelling the products gives the stated extremal constants. The independent 110-digit full Gram diagonalization by direct Taylor coefficient construction for m=1..6 and a=0.01,0.02 confirmed all tested coefficients to within 0.00060 relative error and checked pairing (python3 /workspace/reviews/evidence/reproduce.py 5, requires mpmath).
residual_risks: No uniform large-m conclusion, unequal-multiplicity case or unnormalized derivative statement is proved. The independent finite checks do not prove the asymptotics.
